content.value: Primary reading: Rozanski and Woods, Chapter 23. Supplemental: ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010 architecture description concepts. This unit focuses on architecture reviews and documentation quality.

Architecture review checks whether the architecture description is understandable, complete enough, internally consistent, and useful for its audience. A review also tests whether the architecture supports important quality scenarios.

Documentation quality is judged by use. If stakeholders cannot make decisions, find risks, implement correctly, operate safely, or evaluate tradeoffs, the documentation needs improvement regardless of its length.
Studio: conduct a lightweight review of one architecture view using questions about audience, scope, consistency, risks, and next decisions.

concepts.name: Architecture review
concepts.description: A structured examination of architecture artifacts, decisions, risks, and quality support.

concepts.name: Documentation completeness
concepts.description: The degree to which documentation contains the information stakeholders need for its intended purpose.

concepts.name: Review criterion
concepts.description: A question or standard used to judge architecture quality, documentation quality, or decision adequacy.

concepts.name: Architecture defect
concepts.description: A flaw, omission, inconsistency, or risk in the architecture or its description.
